Neha — quick analysis below. I kept the note short so you can pass it to procurement. Numbers use our hosted list price for rwd-large-v1 = $20.00 per 1M tokens (single blended price for prompt+completion for this exercise).

Assumptions (as agreed):
- Avg per-request: prompt = 1,800 tokens; completion = 700 tokens; total = 2,500 tokens/request.
- Prefix cache only applies to prompt tokens. Completion tokens are always billed.
- Effective billed tokens per request = completion + (1 - hit_rate) * prompt.
- Effective $/1M original tokens = list_price * (billed_tokens_per_request / original_tokens_per_request). This shows what the customer experiences per 1M of their "logical" tokens before caching.

Scenario table (hit rate -> billed tokens per request -> billed/original -> effective $/1M):
- 0% hit:
  billed = 700 + 1.0*1,800 = 2,500 tokens -> billed/original = 1.00 -> effective $/1M = $20.00
- 30% hit:
  billed = 700 + 0.7*1,800 = 1,960 tokens -> billed/original = 0.784 -> effective $/1M = $20.00 * 0.784 = $15.68
- 60% hit:
  billed = 700 + 0.4*1,800 = 1,420 tokens -> billed/original = 0.568 -> effective $/1M = $20.00 * 0.568 = $11.36

Interpretation / recommended offers:
1) Baseline: with no cache (0%) the effective $/1M is $20 — above procurement's band.
2) With a realistic 40% prefix hit (their stated working assumption), you land between the 30% and 60% rows -> interpolate: ~0.676 billed/original -> ~$13.52 per 1M. That is inside their target band ($12–15).
3) To reliably hit procurement stretch ($10/1M) you need ~70%+ prefix hit OR additional list-price concessions (volume tier, dedicated pricing, or using a quantized/dedicated model variant with lower base price).

Quick proposal for Neha to present to procurement: Option A (Simple): show the matrix above plus a committed-volume tier: 20% off list at 75M+ tokens -> pushes effective to ~ $10.95 at 40% hit. Option B (Technical): offer a quantized/dedicated variant (rwd-large-q4) with list price $14/1M — at 40% hit -> effective ~$9.47. Option C: Hybrid — 10% committed discount + recommend customer enable prefix caching on common SOP templates; projected effective ~$11–12 at 40% hit.

Caveats / what doesn't get cached:
- Completion tokens (the generated reply) are never cached and always billed.
- User-specific signals (fresh context like per-user slots, ephemeral conversation data) may not be cacheable depending on their design — call that out in the contract.
- Very large prompts that exceed our prefix normalization window may be only partially cacheable.
